title: Backend Developer Roadmap
description: Become a professional backend developer. Learn how to build APIs, manage databases, handle authentication, and deploy scalable backend applications.

Syllabus.title: Programming Foundations
Syllabus.description: Master a backend programming language and foundational concepts.
Lesson: Choose one: Python, Java, Node.js, Go, Ruby

Syllabus.title: Understanding Web Servers
Syllabus.description: Learn how backend servers handle HTTP requests and responses.
Lesson: How the web works: HTTP, DNS, ports

Syllabus.title: Building APIs
Syllabus.description: Create and manage REST APIs using a backend framework.
Lesson: Setting up a basic server (Flask, Express, Spring Boot)

Syllabus.title: Databases and CRUD
Syllabus.description: Store and manipulate data using databases.

Syllabus.title: Authentication and Security
Syllabus.description: Implement secure user authentication and protect your app.
Lesson: Basic security: CORS, rate limiting, input validation

Syllabus.title: Middleware and Error Handling
Syllabus.description: Manage request flow and exceptions effectively.
Lesson: Error handling and custom error responses

Syllabus.title: Async Programming and Background Jobs
Syllabus.description: Perform non-blocking tasks and schedule background jobs.

Syllabus.title: Testing and Debugging
Syllabus.description: Ensure your backend is reliable and bug-free.
Lesson: Unit and integration testing (e.g., pytest, JUnit, Jest)

Syllabus.title: File Handling and Storage
Syllabus.description: Manage file uploads and external storage.
Lesson: Saving files to disk or cloud (S3, Cloudinary)

Syllabus.title: WebSockets and Real-Time Communication
Syllabus.description: Enable real-time features like chat or live updates.

Syllabus.title: Deployment and DevOps Basics
Syllabus.description: Take your backend app to production.
Lesson: Deploying to services like Render, Railway, DigitalOcean, or AWS

Syllabus.title: Scalability and Best Practices
Syllabus.description: Write clean, scalable, and maintainable backend code.
Lesson: Monitoring and logging (e.g., Prometheus, ELK stack)
